title: The Protection Threshold: When Flops End Hollywood’s Silence
audience: Readers who want a citable, data-framed answer to “why not sooner?” — commercial value, institutional risk, and timelines — not true-crime spectacle.
metaDescription: BBC’s Jared Leto exposé raises “why not sooner?” We test whether box-office decline, dual film/music books, and institutional risk mark a protection threshold.
angle: News peg is the BBC Leto documentary; the Artometrics move is economic — measure film ROI, music durability, pre-exposé studio health (Weinstein), and false rehab signals (Singer / Bohemian Rhapsody), with Savile and Brand as broadcaster counterexamples.

distribution.linkedinHook: The question after the BBC’s Jared Leto film isn’t only moral — it’s economic: how cheap does someone have to become before institutions stop protecting them?
distribution.shortFact: Test case: Leto’s 2020s tentpoles vs music touring; Weinstein’s pre-2017 slump; Singer’s Bohemian Rhapsody credit without rehab.
